source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Aspirated objects most often lodge in the right lung because the right main bronchus is:
questions.rationale: The right bronchus is shorter, broader and more vertical, so aspiration and infection more often affect the right lung.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Anatomy (PDF p. 40)
questions.quote: The right bronchus is shorter, broader, and more vertical.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In a healthy person, the main chemical stimulus to breathe is:
questions.rationale: Central chemoreceptors in the medulla respond mainly to high CO2; peripheral receptors respond to low O2.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Respiratory centers (PDF p. 40)
questions.quote: The main chemical stimulus for breathing is high levels of carbon dioxide in the blood.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A high-pitched, musical sound heard mainly on expiration is a:
questions.rationale: Wheezes are continuous high-pitched musical sounds on expiration; crackles are discontinuous pops.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Adventitious breath sounds (PDF p. 42)
questions.quote: Continuous, high-pitched, hissing (musical) on expiration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A Mantoux test is read after:
questions.rationale: PPD is given intradermally and read at 48–72 hours; ≥10 mm induration is positive (≥5 mm if HIV-positive).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Mantoux test (PDF p. 43)
questions.quote: Read result 48-72 hours after injection.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: For a client with HIV, what Mantoux induration is considered positive?
questions.rationale: For HIV-positive clients, 5 mm induration is positive; 10 mm for the general population.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Mantoux test (PDF p. 43)
questions.quote: For HIV positive clients, induration of 5 mm is considered positive.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After bronchoscopy, when may the client drink?
questions.rationale: Throat anesthesia abolishes the gag reflex; keep NPO and side-lying until it returns to prevent aspiration.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 After bronchoscopy (PDF p. 44)
questions.quote: Check for the return of gag reflex before giving fluid per orem.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Mang Ben, admitted for suspected pneumonia, is due for a sputum culture. When and how should it be collected?
questions.rationale: Early morning sputum is most plentiful; collect before antibiotics, rinse with plain water, use a sterile container.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Sputum examination (PDF p. 45)
questions.quote: Sputum specimen for C & S is collected before the first dose of antimicrobial.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before drawing an arterial blood gas from the radial artery, the nurse performs Allen's test to check:
questions.rationale: Allen's test confirms adequate collateral (ulnar) flow to the hand; color should return within about 6 seconds.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Arterial blood gas studies (PDF p. 46)
questions.quote: Allen's test is done to assess for adequacy of collateral circulation of the hand.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During thoracentesis, the client is best positioned:
questions.rationale: Upright and leaning forward on a table spreads the ribs and lets fluid settle for aspiration.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Thoracentesis (PDF p. 46)
questions.quote: Position: upright, leaning on overbed table, feet supported on foot stooL

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which oxygen device delivers the highest concentration in an emergency?
questions.rationale: A non-rebreather at 10–15 L/min gives about 95–100%; nasal cannula gives 24–44%.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Oxygen therapy (PDF p. 47)
questions.quote: The non-breather face mask is the most effective method of oxygen delivery.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A COPD client needs an exact, controlled oxygen concentration. The best device is a:
questions.rationale: The Venturi mask delivers accurate FiO2, preferred for clients who retain CO2; titrate to target saturation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Oxygen therapy (PDF p. 47)
questions.quote: Use venturi mask for clients with COPD

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When suctioning a tracheostomy, suction is applied:
questions.rationale: Apply suction on withdrawal for 10–15 seconds max, hyperoxygenating before and after, using sterile technique.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Tracheostomy suctioning (PDF p. 47)
questions.quote: Apply suction or negative pressure during withdrawal of catheter

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During suctioning the heart rate drops from 88 to 52. This is due to:
questions.rationale: Over-suctioning can cause hypoxia and vagal stimulation, seen as bradycardia and hypotension; stop and oxygenate.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Tracheostomy suctioning (PDF p. 47)
questions.quote: Vagal stimulation is manifested by bradycardia and hypotension.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Chest physiotherapy is best scheduled:
questions.rationale: Postural drainage is done before meals and on waking, after bronchodilator treatment, to avoid vomiting and aid expectoration.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Chest physiotherapy (PDF p. 48)
questions.quote: The procedure is best done before meals, upon awakening in the morning

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In a chest drainage unit, continuous bubbling in the water-seal chamber means:
options: An air leak in the system
questions.rationale: Water-seal should fluctuate with breathing, not bubble continuously; constant bubbling signals an air leak.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Chest tube drainage (PDF p. 48)
questions.quote: Bubbling in the water-seal chamber indicates air leak in the system.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The chest drainage bottle breaks. The nurse's first action is to:
options: Submerge the tube end in sterile water
Clamp the tube for an hour
Raise the tube above the chest
questions.rationale: Immerse the tubing end in sterile saline or water to restore a water seal; prolonged clamping risks tension pneumothorax.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Chest tube drainage (PDF p. 49)
questions.quote: If closed drainage system is broken, immerse end of tubing in normal saline or glass of water. Do not clamp.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A ventilator's high-pressure alarm sounds. The most common cause is:
questions.rationale: High pressure = obstruction (secretions, kinks, biting the tube); low pressure = disconnection or leak.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Ventilator alarms (PDF p. 49)
questions.quote: O — Obstruction (mucuous secretions, kink in the tubing, client bites on the endotracheal tube)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A ventilator keeps alarming after suctioning and checking connections. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: If the cause can't be fixed, disconnect and ventilate with a manual resuscitation bag.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 ARDS and ventilators (PDF p. 56)
questions.quote: disconnect client from ventilator and do manual ventilation (Ambu bag)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which position helps stop an anterior nosebleed?
questions.rationale: Leaning forward prevents swallowing and aspiration of blood; apply pressure and cold.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Epistaxis (PDF p. 49)
questions.quote: The best position of the client is sitting up, leaning forward

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After tonsillectomy, which sign suggests bleeding?
questions.rationale: Frequent swallowing signals bleeding; avoid straws, red fluids, milk and irritating foods.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Tonsillectomy (PDF p. 50)
questions.quote: Frequent swallowing indicates bleeding.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why are drinking straws avoided after tonsillectomy?
questions.rationale: Sucking through a straw can dislodge the clot at the operative site and cause bleeding.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Tonsillectomy (PDF p. 50)
questions.quote: Blood clot in the operative area may be dislodged as the client sucks through the straw.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After total laryngectomy, the client will permanently lose the ability to:
questions.rationale: Total laryngectomy causes loss of voice, a permanent tracheostomy, loss of smell and inability to do Valsalva.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Cancer of the larynx (PDF p. 51)
questions.quote: The client will have permanent tracheostomy, loss of sense of smell, and unable to do Valsalva maneuver.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the earliest sign of laryngeal cancer?
questions.rationale: Persistent hoarseness is the initial manifestation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Cancer of the larynx (PDF p. 51)
questions.quote: The initial manifestation of cancer of the larynx is persistent hoarseness of voice.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A COPD client asks why his diet should be lower in carbohydrates. The nurse explains carbohydrates:
questions.rationale: CO2 is the end product of carbohydrate metabolism; COPD clients already retain CO2. Diet is high calorie and protein.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 COPD (PDF p. 51)
questions.quote: Low carbohydrate diet prevents excessive formation of carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client uses an inhaled bronchodilator and an inhaled steroid. Which teaching is correct?
questions.rationale: The bronchodilator opens airways so the steroid reaches deeper; rinse after the steroid to prevent thrush.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Pharmacotherapy for COPD (PDF p. 52)
questions.quote: Bronchodilator inhalation should be given before steroid inhalation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An asthmatic's peak flow is 60% of her personal best. She is in which zone?
questions.rationale: Green 80–100%, yellow 50–80% (caution, use prescribed medication), red <50% (medical alert).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Peak flow meter (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: 50 to 80% of your usual or "normal" peak flow rate signals caution.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug class can trigger asthma attacks?
questions.rationale: Aspirin, NSAIDs and beta-adrenergic blockers are known asthma triggers.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Asthma triggers (PDF p. 53)
questions.quote: Beta — adrenergic blockers

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A tension pneumothorax shifts the trachea toward the:
questions.rationale: Pneumothorax causes mediastinal shift toward the unaffected side, with absent breath sounds on the affected side.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Pneumothorax (PDF p. 55)
questions.quote: Pneumothorax is accompanied by mediastinal shift (deviation of larynx and trachea) to the unaffected side.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After pneumonectomy, the client is positioned:
questions.rationale: Turning slightly to the operative side lets the remaining lung expand; no chest tube is usually placed.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Thoracic surgeries (PDF p. 55)
questions.quote: Best postop position is Semi Fowler's slightly turned to the affected side.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on isoniazid is given vitamin B6 to prevent:
questions.rationale: Pyridoxine prevents INH-induced peripheral neuritis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Tuberculosis (PDF p. 56)
questions.quote: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) is administered to prevent INH-induced peripheral neuritis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on ethambutol should be advised to have:
questions.rationale: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis (visual acuity, red-green color changes).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Tuberculosis (PDF p. 56)
questions.quote: Ethambutol causes optic neuritis. The client is advised to have periodic eye examination.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A crushed-chest patient's chest wall moves in on inspiration and out on expiration. This is:
questions.rationale: Flail chest (two or more adjacent rib fractures) produces paradoxical chest movement.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Flail chest (PDF p. 57)
questions.quote: It is characterized by paradoxical breathing chest segment moves inward during inspiration and outward during expiration.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A bedridden client after hip surgery suddenly has severe dyspnea, pleuritic pain and anxiety. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: PE from venous stasis presents with sudden dyspnea, sharp pleuritic pain, restlessness and possibly hemoptysis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 Pulmonary embolism (PDF p. 57)
questions.quote: Characteristic manifestations are sudden severe dyspnea, restlessness, anxiety, sharp pleuritic pain

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: ABG: pH 7.30, PaCO2 52 mmHg, HCO3 24 mEq/L. This is:
questions.rationale: Low pH with high PaCO2 (opposite directions) and normal HCO3 = uncompensated respiratory acidosis (ROME).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 3 ABG analysis (PDF p. 61)
questions.quote: Respiratory Opposite means: the directions of pH and paC02 are opposite.
